input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay commitment on Customer with no reduction or termination rights. Because Customer must pay the full amount regardless of Services consumed and regardless of any termination, the provision operates as a Customer-payable minimum fee/penalty (effectively liquidated damages for the remaining contract value), which the playbook prohibits. It also contradicts Section 7.1 (no undisclosed minimum-use charge) and Section 12.3 (Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment). No other Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalty exists in the document; Sections 7.3, 19.4 and 27.3 run in our favour. The redline deletes the take-or-pay penalty and, per the fallback, confirms that any early-termination fee is capped at three months' Fees as the sole liquidated amount.

ops.oldText: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: Customer has no minimum purchase, take-or-pay, or minimum-fee commitment and shall pay only for Services actually ordered under an Order Form. Customer shall not owe any liquidated damages, penalty, or termination charge, and if an Order Form provides for an early-termination fee, that fee is Customer's sole liability and shall not exceed three months' Fees for the terminated Services.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the take-or-pay minimum, which operates as a liquidated penalty payable by us and conflicts with Sections 7.1 and 12.3, and confirmed that any early-termination fee is capped at three months' Fees as the sole liquidated amount.
proposal.summary: Delete Customer take-or-pay penalty; cap any early-termination fee at three months' Fees.
